name: Automated compliance

subjectOf.text: When decentralization at the Layer 1 level is compromised, the autonomy of the smart contracts deployed on that chain is compromised by affiliation, so smart contracts are corruptible in the current design and cannot reliably serve as neutral instruments of ethical AI governance.
subjectOf.abstract: When the decentralization of Layer 1 blockchains is compromised, the autonomy of smart contracts is inherently jeopardized, undermining their effectiveness as tools for ethical AI governance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4796714
scope_conditions: applies where a few dominant parties influence the underlying Layer 1
holds under current blockchain design as of 2024

subjectOf.text: Smart contracts can automate compliance with regulatory requirements and ethical guidelines: for example, a smart contract can enforce privacy law directly by controlling an AI system's access to personal data according to predefined rules.
subjectOf.abstract: They can be used to automate compliance with regulatory requirements and ethical guidelines. For instance, smart contracts can automatically enforce privacy laws by controlling AI's access to personal data based on predefined rules.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Governance Via Web3 Reputation System (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4941807
scope_conditions: where compliance rules can be expressed as predefined, codified conditions

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'automated-compliance'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
